cases.statement: One carrier: Patient 2 of PMID 34030699, a girl aged 11 years 7 months with axial spinal arthritis, recurrent oral ulcers, lupus-like autoimmunity and short stature; heterozygous; reported as a spontaneous mutation. The review 39125844 (Table 2 row 1) summarises the same girl, citing PMID 34030699 as [31].

people.label: Patient 2
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent lower back pain with axial/spinal arthritis (thoracic kyphosis, scoliosis); recurrent oral ulcers; lupus-like autoimmunity (ANA, SSA, dsDNA, Coombs positive; autoimmune haemolytic anaemia); short stature ('dwarfism'); alopecia

quotes.quote: An 11 years and 7 months girl was admitted with “recurrent lower back pain for over two years”.
Over 2 years before admission, her patient discovered that the girl had thoracic kyphosis and recurrent oral ulcers.
Enhanced MRI of thoracic and lumbar spine at our hospital revealed extensive small pyramidal arthritic changes (Fig. 3).
Together with her presentation of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and arthritis, a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus was considered in accordance with the 1997 ACR standard.
Since her height was only 130 cm at age 11, which is below the 3rd percentile for the same sex and age, she was diagnosed with dwarfism.

This mutation was observed in an 11-year-old child with recurrent lower back pain and recurrent ulcers.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors describe Patient 2 as mainly autoimmune (spinal arthritis and lupus-like syndrome) without fever or gastrointestinal symptoms, unlike the Behçet-like picture of their Patient 3. She was HLA-B27 positive, which the authors do not discuss. Whole-exome sequencing with frequency and in-silico filtering was used; no other candidate variant is reported.

quotes.quote: Patient 2 had no fever or gastrointestinal symptoms but was positive for ANA, SSA, dsDNA, and Coombs test, and exhibited severe spinal arthritis and lupus-like syndrome, which are characteristic of autoimmune diseases.
Rheumatoid factor (RF) examination at local hospital was 37.5 IU/mL, positivity for HLA-B27, normal WBC, CRP of 42.7 mg/L, and AESR of 50 mm/60 min,.
The SNPs and indels obtained from screening had a frequency of less than 0.05 in the 1000 Genomes Project, ESP6500si, ExAC_ALL, ExAC_EAS, and the myGenostics 1000 normal individual databases.

de_novo.statement: The paper calls the variant a 'spontaneous mutation' confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and states blood was collected from each child and their parents (Fig. 3 shows maps for Patient 2's father and mother). It does not state in words that both parents lacked the variant, and parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: c.1906 + 1G > C and c.925_927dup were confirmed by Sanger sequencing as spontaneous mutations.

After obtaining consent from the child’s guardian, approximately 2 mL (EDTA anticoagulant) of peripheral blood was collected from each child and their parents, and genomic DNA was extracted using the QIAamp whole blood DNA extraction kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany).
**Fig. 3**: a Map of gene mutations of Patient 2. b Map of gene mutations of Patient 2’s father. c map of gene mutations of Patient 2’s mother

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice donor variant (+1); predicted protein p.? per the batch HGVS. The authors suggest only that it may affect splicing (no RNA study). The paper attributes HA20 to insufficient A20 production.

quotes.quote: Among them, 1906 + 1G > C may affect the alternative splicing of exons, thereby affecting protein function.
The cause of this disease is insufficient production of A20 resulting in negative feedback inhibition of NF-kB signalling pathway.

computational_predictions.statement: GERP++ placed the site in a conserved region. The methods mention SIFT, PolyPhen2 and MutationTaster as filters, but no variant-specific scores are given.

quotes.quote: Among these mutations, c.1906 + 1G > C and c.547C > T were predicted by GERP++ as loci in a conserved region.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Stated absent from 1000 Genomes, ESP6500si, ExAC (all and East Asian) and a 1000-person in-house control set.

quotes.quote: All of those mutations do not appear in 1000 Genomes Project, ESP6500si, ExAC_ALL, ExAC_EAS, or myGenostics 1000 normal individual databases.

authors_classification.statement: The authors state only a 'possibility of pathogenicity at genetic level'. No ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: Based on these results, our 3 patients showed the possibility of pathogenicity at genetic level.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on renal involvement: Table 1 marks 'Renal damage' + for Patient 2, but the text says her urine tests and 24-h urinary protein were normal and no renal biopsy was done.
Figure numbering is inconsistent: the text says 'see Fig. 4' for Patient 2's mutation map, but the Fig. 4 legend is for Patient 3 and the Fig. 3 legend is for Patient 2.
'Spontaneous mutation' is read by the pipeline as de novo; the text does not say in words that both parents lacked it.
39125844 (review) is a secondary summary of the same girl, not an independent case. It gives onset 10 years in the table and says 'There were no joint issues' while also listing arthritis.
Transcript not stated (reference genome hg19 for alignment); the batch uses NM_001270508.2.
Same splice donor site as G-ha20-053 (c.1906+2T>G, PMID 35958611), which has RNA and protein data from patient cells; the panel may want to read the two together.
notes_for_panel: Single proband with a canonical +1 donor change, reported as spontaneous; no RNA or functional study. The phenotype (axial arthritis, lupus-like autoimmunity) is less typical, and the patient is HLA-B27 positive.
